conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. I know this has been a scary night. You had trouble breathing and turned blue, but the team helped you and you're safe now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Mmm… blue?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you stopped breathing for a bit. EMS suctioned a large mucus plug from your trach tube. That’s likely what caused it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Trach… stuck again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. You’ve had this happen before. We’re keeping a close eye on your secretions and suctioning as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Lungs… okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did a CT scan. You have patchy areas in your lungs—likely pneumonia or aspiration. We’re starting antibiotics just in case.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Antibiotics… again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, because we found signs of infection. We also took a sputum sample to check what kind of bacteria are there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Fever?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No fever now. Your white count is a bit high, which supports infection, but you’re stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your sputum culture came back. You have Pseudomonas and Proteus in your lungs.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Pseudo… what?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Two types of bacteria. Pseudomonas is common in patients with trachs. We’re adjusting your antibiotics to cover both.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Need IV?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we placed a PICC line yesterday so you can get IV antibiotics safely. It’ll help you finish treatment at your care facility.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: PICC… okay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also found yeast in your urine. It’s likely from your catheter. We’re changing the catheter and starting fluconazole.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeast? Like… fungus?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, a type of fungal infection. It’s treatable. We’ll give you oral medication for 13 days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No pain… just tired.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. You had a big scare. Your body’s healing. We’re watching your oxygen and lungs closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your latest chest X-ray shows improvement. The collapse in your lower lobes is getting better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good… breathing easier.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and your oxygen levels are stable on lower support. That’s a great sign.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Med changes?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re increasing your gabapentin for leg pain and baclofen for muscle tightness. Also adding senna for constipation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay… stomach okay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your repeat urine culture still shows yeast, so we’re continuing fluconazole. No change there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Still need it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, to fully clear the infection. We don’t want it coming back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: INR?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your INR was 3.0 on admission—too high. We held Coumadin briefly. Now we’re restarting it at 4 mg daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Bleeding?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly at your trach site. The nursing staff noted some bleeding. We’ll monitor your INR closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Check again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll check it before you leave. You’ll need heparin shots until it’s above 2.0.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great news—your chest X-ray today shows even more improvement. Your lungs are clearing well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Feel better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad. We’re almost ready to send you back to extended care. You’ll finish antibiotics there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Which ones?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Levofloxacin and cefpodoxime for pneumonia, fluconazole for yeast. You’ll take them for several more days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: PICC care?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your care team will flush it daily and give antibiotics through it. They’ll be trained before discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Wound?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your sacral ulcer is stage I—stable. Keep turning regularly and we’ll send supplies for care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing really well. We’re discharging you today to extended care. You’ve recovered from the respiratory arrest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Continue all meds, especially the antibiotics and fluconazole. Watch for fever or trouble breathing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: INR check?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, check INR on the scheduled day. Call your doctor for Coumadin dose adjustments.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your care team will coordinate follow-up. If anything changes, they’ll reach out.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay… ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve made great progress. Keep up the good work. We’ll send all instructions to your facility.
